page: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Famdsv7 family. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The CPU includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions (AVX512_VNNI). The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores all placing in the top 10%. However, multi-core scaling is more moderate; stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average range. Memory bandwidth is average, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 420.17 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 30.22 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and static web serving throughput are weaker, placing in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is poor, though small-model (135M) inference achieves average speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F2amds_v7 offers a high-frequency, dedicated-core AMD hardware profile with a generous memory allocation relative to its low vCPU count, making it a resource-dense option without the overhead of larger instances. Given the strong single-core performance and memory capacity, this server is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallelization, such as lightweight database operations, single-threaded data processing, text processing, and small-scale model inference.
